material_systems.name: Vinyl Adhesion Primer (STIX Class)

primer.type: High-solids adhesion primer — solvent-attack chemical bond to PVC
products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start All-Purpose Primer (023)
primer.notes: MANDATORY for all vinyl siding repaints. These formulations 'bite' into PVC via solvent attack, creating a chemical bond rather than relying on mechanical adhesion alone. Standard exterior primers, bonding primers for glossy latex, and all-purpose primers are NOT acceptable substitutes. Full-surface coverage required — no spot priming option. Vinyl's smooth factory finish provides consistent coverage.

applies_when.condition: always — adhesion primer is mandatory regardless of vinyl condition

material_systems.notes: Single primer system for vinyl. No state-dependent primer branching (unlike wood siding repaint with 5 primer systems). Adhesion primer serves adhesion function ONLY — no stain-blocking needed (vinyl has no tannins or extractive bleeding).

material_systems.name: Exterior Acrylic Latex — Standard Colors (LRV 55+)

finish.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior latex for colors with LRV 55 or higher. QT2 = single finish coat (economy). QT3 = two finish coats (standard residential). Binder MUST be 100% acrylic latex — alkyd, oil-based, and hybrid formulations are PROHIBITED on vinyl (crack/delaminate within 12-24 months due to PVC thermal movement). Verify binder type on PDS before approving any product.

material_systems.notes: Standard color path. Any color with LRV >= 55 qualifies. No thermal distortion risk at this LRV range. Widest product selection available.

material_systems.name: Exterior IR-Reflective Acrylic — Dark Colors (LRV 35-55)

finish.type: 100% Acrylic Exterior Latex with IR-Reflective Pigments
products: Benjamin Moore Colors for Vinyl (Regal Select Exterior line)
PPG Timeless Exterior with VinylSafe Technology
finish.notes: IR-reflective pigment technology allows darker colors (LRV 35-55) on vinyl siding without exceeding PVC heat deflection threshold (165 degrees F). IR-reflective pigments reflect near-infrared radiation, reducing surface temperature gain by 20-40%. Coverage is 15-20% lower than standard acrylic due to heavier specialty pigment load. MUST verify IR-reflective claim on PDS — not all dark-base paints contain IR-reflective pigments. Binder MUST be 100% acrylic latex.

material_systems.notes: Specialty color path for darker tones. Higher material cost per gallon than standard acrylic but does NOT change labor time. Limited color palette compared to standard path — only colors validated as IR-reflective by manufacturer. South/west facades at highest thermal risk even with IR-reflective products.

SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT.notes: Vinyl factory finish is smooth and non-porous. Consistent coverage across all panels. Aged/UV-chalked vinyl (after washing) may absorb slightly more primer — use lower end of range for visibly chalked surfaces.

assumptions: Full-surface coverage required — adhesion primer must bond to entire PVC surface.
Coverage based on NET siding area from PaintScope (PS_EXT_SURFACE_SF.SIDING_FIELD).
Single coat only. Do not double-coat adhesion primer — excessive film build reduces flexibility.

lap_horizontal.notes: Standard vinyl lap siding. Smooth factory profile over primed surface. Best coverage rate.

dutch_lap.notes: Dutch lap has a concave profile that adds ~5-10% effective area vs flat lap.

board_and_batten.notes: Vinyl board-and-batten. Effective area ~1.10x net due to batten profiles (less deep than wood equivalent at 1.20x).

shake_shingle.notes: Vinyl shake/shingle panels. Textured surface with many edges increases material consumption ~15% vs smooth lap.

assumptions: Coverage is per NET siding area from PaintScope.
Primed surface (adhesion primer coat applied) provides consistent base — repaint coverage slightly better than first-time paint on raw vinyl.
QT2 = single coat. QT3 = two coats (multiply gallon estimate by coat count).

lap_horizontal.notes: IR-reflective pigment load reduces coverage 15-20% vs standard acrylic. Heavier pigment requires more material per SF.

dutch_lap.notes: Dutch lap profile + IR-reflective pigment load. Combined coverage reduction.

shake_shingle.notes: Vinyl shake/shingle with IR-reflective product. Highest material consumption profile.

assumptions: IR-reflective products have higher pigment density — lower coverage per gallon is expected.
Coverage rates are conservative estimates based on PDS ranges for VinylSafe-class products.
QT2 = single coat. QT3 = two coats.

consumables.name: Airless spray tips 413-515
consumables.notes: 413 tip for adhesion primer (lower viscosity). 515 tip for finish coat. Replace when fan pattern deteriorates.

consumables.name: Airless sprayer filters (gun and manifold)
consumables.notes: Gun filter and manifold filter. Clean between primer and finish. Replace when clogging causes pressure spikes.

consumables.name: Brushes 2-3 inch for J-channel detail
consumables.notes: 2 inch for J-channels and under-sill channels. 3 inch for siding-to-trim cut-in. QT3 detail work.

consumables.name: TSP cleaner / alkaline siding wash
consumables.notes: Trisodium phosphate or dedicated vinyl siding cleaner concentrate. Mix per manufacturer directions. Required for chalk, mildew, and dirt removal before priming.

consumables.name: Pressure washer tips (25-40 degree fan)
consumables.notes: 25-degree tip for siding field wash. 40-degree for delicate areas. 500-1000 PSI — do NOT exceed 1500 PSI on vinyl (can force water behind panels at joints).

consumables.name: Synthetic scuff pads (180-320 grit equivalent)
consumables.notes: Light scuff for adhesion tooth on smooth vinyl surface. Synthetic pads preferred over sandpaper — won't tear on vinyl lap edges. Minimal prep vs wood siding scraping.

consumables.name: Siliconized acrylic exterior caulk
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: QT3 only. Paintable siliconized acrylic for siding-to-trim joints. Vinyl has low joint movement — polyurethane not required. Estimate 50-100 LF per typical residential project.

consumables.name: Masking tape (exterior grade UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum. Blue tape for trim transitions. Red stucco poly tape (30-day UV) for extended spray masking on high-adhesion surfaces.

consumables.name: Masking paper / kraft paper 12-18 inch
consumables.notes: For masking windows, doors, and trim during spray application. Paper + tape machine application for speed.

consumables.name: Pre-taped masking film (hand-masker rolls)
consumables.notes: Pre-taped plastic film for window and door masking. Faster than paper + tape for full-cover window masking during spray.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting 4 mil
consumables.notes: Landscape, hardscape, and fixture protection during spray. 4 mil minimum — thinner tears on shrubs and rough surfaces.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Reusable canvas drops along foundation perimeter for drip protection during wash and spray.

compatibility_rules.description: Adhesion primer ALWAYS required — no skip-prime option
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY. Standard exterior primers do not bond to vinyl's low surface energy PVC. Adhesion primer (STIX class) creates chemical bond via solvent attack. No exceptions, no state-dependent branching.
Any 100% acrylic exterior latex qualifies. No thermal distortion risk at LRV >= 55. Widest product and color selection.

compatibility_rules.description: IR-reflective finish REQUIRED for LRV 35-55 colors
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY. Colors with LRV 35-55 MUST use IR-reflective pigment products. Standard acrylic in this LRV range will cause thermal distortion on vinyl. Verify IR-reflective claim on manufacturer PDS.

then.reason: No material system available for colors below LRV 35 on vinyl siding. Even IR-reflective pigments cannot prevent thermal distortion at this LRV range. PVC heat deflection temperature (165 degrees F) will be exceeded. Damage is irreversible — warped panels require replacement.

compatibility_rules.notes: ABSOLUTE GATE. No override, no exception. Estimation engine must reject any color selection below LRV 35 on vinyl siding.

then.reason: Alkyd, oil-based, and hybrid coatings lack flexibility to accommodate PVC thermal movement (up to 5/8 inch per 12-ft panel). Coating will crack and delaminate within 12-24 months. Only 100% acrylic latex is permitted on vinyl siding.

compatibility_rules.notes: ABSOLUTE CONSTRAINT. Enforced at material specification level. QC verification at material delivery. If wrong product arrives on site, do NOT apply — return and reorder.
Economy tier. Single finish coat over adhesion primer. Acceptable for budget-constrained work, rental property, pre-sale cosmetic refresh. Shorter maintenance cycle than 2-coat system.

compatibility_rules.description: QT3 — two finish coats + detail work
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard residential tier. Two finish coats for full hide, proper film build, and maximum durability. Brush detail at J-channels, under-sill channels, and trim cut-in. Caulk assessment at siding-to-trim joints.

then.reason: Cracked, warped, broken, or physically damaged vinyl panels cannot be painted. PVC damage is structural — painting cannot restore panel integrity. Panels must be replaced by siding contractor before painting scope applies.

compatibility_rules.notes: Vinyl condition is binary: sound (repaintable) or damaged (replacement scope). No intermediate state.

risk_notes.description: Colors below LRV 55 without IR-reflective pigments will cause PVC surface temperature to exceed heat deflection threshold (165 degrees F). Vinyl panels permanently warp, buckle, or distort. Damage is irreversible — panels must be replaced.
risk_notes.mitigation: LRV restriction enforced by COMPAT_VNRP_002, COMPAT_VNRP_003, COMPAT_VNRP_004. Standard colors LRV 55+. IR-reflective only for LRV 35-55. Hard stop below LRV 35.

risk_notes.topic: Coating failure from wrong binder type
risk_notes.description: Alkyd, oil, or hybrid coatings will crack and delaminate from vinyl within 12-24 months. PVC thermal expansion (5/8 inch per 12-ft panel) exceeds the flexibility of non-acrylic binders. Complete system failure requiring full strip and repaint.
risk_notes.mitigation: Binder lock enforced by COMPAT_VNRP_005. 100% acrylic latex ONLY. QC verification at material delivery.

risk_notes.topic: Adhesion failure from skipping or substituting adhesion primer
risk_notes.description: Standard exterior primers, bonding primers for glossy surfaces, and all-purpose primers do NOT chemically bond to PVC. Without STIX-class adhesion primer, entire coating system peels from vinyl in sheets at expansion joints.
risk_notes.mitigation: Mandatory adhesion primer enforced by COMPAT_VNRP_001. STIX class only — no substitution.

risk_notes.description: Painting vinyl siding voids manufacturer finish warranty (CertainTeed, Mastic, Westlake Royal all explicitly state this). Client must acknowledge warranty void before work proceeds. Contractor provides 5-10 year workmanship warranty in lieu of manufacturer coverage.
risk_notes.mitigation: Warranty void acknowledgment gate in SOP — client sign-off required before any work begins.

risk_notes.description: UV-degraded vinyl releases chalk powder. If adhesion primer is applied over chalk residue, primer bonds to chalk rather than PVC. Patchy peeling results.
risk_notes.mitigation: Mandatory pressure wash with alkaline cleaner removes chalk. Hand-rub test after drying to verify removal. Re-wash if chalk persists.

risk_notes.topic: IR-reflective products on south/west facades in extreme heat
risk_notes.description: Even with IR-reflective pigments, dark colors (LRV 35-55) on high-solar-exposure facades may approach thermal limits during extreme heat events. Temporary panel buckling during peak heat with potential for progressive permanent deformation.
risk_notes.mitigation: Recommend lighter colors (LRV 55+) on south/west facades when possible. Document exposure risk in client warranty disclosure. IR-reflective products reduce but do not eliminate thermal risk.

assumptions.value: 350 SF/gal baseline on smooth vinyl factory finish
assumptions.note: Vinyl is smooth and non-porous — higher primer coverage than wood siding. Lower end (300 SF/gal) for visibly chalked surfaces.

assumptions.value: 15-20% lower coverage vs standard acrylic due to heavier pigment load
assumptions.source: Researcher analysis based on VinylSafe PDS data
assumptions.note: No doctrine coverage for IR-reflective coverage rates. Derived from manufacturer PDS comparison. Conservative estimate.

assumptions.value: 1.05-1.10x effective area vs flat lap due to concave profile
assumptions.source: Researcher analysis — vinyl dutch lap profile depth
assumptions.note: No doctrine coverage for dutch lap area multiplier. Estimated from profile geometry. Less impact than board-and-batten (1.10x) or shake (1.15x).

assumptions.value: RRP/lead-safe consumables excluded — vinyl siding is post-1960s, never lead-painted
assumptions.note: Factory PVC finish is integral to material, not a paint coating. EPA RRP does not apply.

uncertainty_flags.detail: LRV 35 used as hard stop, but manufacturer-specific IR-reflective thresholds may vary. Some products may allow LRV 32-35; others may require LRV 40+.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Use LRV 35 as conservative hard stop. Defer to specific product PDS for edge cases in 35-40 range.

uncertainty_flags.detail: Coverage rates for vinyl shake/shingle profiles are estimated from textured surface analogies. Limited PDS data specific to vinyl shake panels.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Use lower end of range for vinyl shake profiles. Field calibration recommended.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Adhesion primer on previously painted vinyl
uncertainty_flags.detail: This spec addresses first repaint of factory vinyl. If vinyl has been previously painted (second repaint), adhesion primer behavior may differ — the STIX solvent-attack bond targets PVC, not a previous paint layer. Second-repaint scenarios may need different primer approach.
uncertainty_flags.recommendation: Flag for future spec variant (SF_SIDING_VINYL_EXT_RP_v2 or second-repaint modifier) if demand warrants.
